newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, China start two-day oil conference.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, China start two-day oil conference.

text.p: Oil officials and executives from rivals Taiwan and China opened a two-day forum in southern Taiwan on Tuesday, but the island's oil monopoly said a stalled joint exploration project would not be discussed.

More than 200 participants were to exchange views at the 1997 Cross-Strait Petrochemical Environmental Technology Conference in Kaohsiung, said Ho Li-chun of Taiwan's oil monopoly, Chinese Petroleum Corp, the event's sponsor.

"This is a purely academic seminar. We should discuss nothing other than oil technology," Ho said by telephone, adding that participants would mainly discuss research papers, not cooperation projects.
The 12-strong mainland China delegation includes officials from Beijing's China Petrochemical Corp, China National Petrochemical Corp and China National Offshore Oil Corp.

The gathering marks the first face-to-face meeting of Taiwan and China oil officials since July 1996, when Chinese Petroleum signed a landmark accord with Beijing's China National Offshore Oil Corp for future cooperation.

The pact, allowing joint research and preparations for oil exploration between south China's Pearl River delta and the Taiwan strait, was stalled by Chinese Petroleum after Taiwan's government called for toned down economic links with China.
Taiwan has not changed its go-slow position, Ho said.
"We have no immediate plan to resume discussions with the mainland side on the joint exploration project," Ho said.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949. But a political thaw in the late 1980s has allowed commercial and other unofficial cross-strait ties to flourish.
Taiwan, worried that its economy may become too dependent on China, began urging local firms in mid-1996 to slow investments in the communist mainland.
